title: Sponge, funnel, strainer, sieve (Avot 5:15)
hook: four kinds of students; the sieve lets the dust through and keeps the fine flour
tomorrow: Owen got in, far away. does a friendship survive that?

segments.voice: Last week closed on give and invite: the chasid gives and makes room for others to give. This week opens on what you keep.

The run-through ends. The cast sits on the edge of the stage, and the director flips open a legal pad: a whole page of notes. Four actors listen. The first writes down every word, the jokes, the asides, the cough. The second nods at everything and has forgotten all of it by the parking lot. The third hears one sharp note about her timing and replays it all night, while the praise slides off. The fourth listens, crosses out half, and circles two lines. So, a whole page of notes: which ones do you keep?
screen: `A WHOLE PAGE OF NOTES.` → `FOUR ACTORS, FOUR WAYS.` → `WHICH ONES DO YOU KEEP?`

segments.voice: Avot got there first, with kitchen tools. There are four kinds among those who sit before the sages: a sponge, a funnel, a strainer and a sieve. The sponge soaks up everything. The funnel takes it in one end and lets it out the other. The strainer lets the wine run out and keeps the dregs. The sieve lets the flour dust fall through and keeps the fine flour. That's the four actors. The note-taker who keeps every cough: sponge. The nodder: funnel, the old picture of in one ear and out the other. The one replaying the single sharp note: strainer, holding on to the dregs while the wine runs away. And the one with two circled lines: sieve. Here's the twist. The sponge sounds like the star student. It keeps everything. But it keeps everything, the good and the grit together, and can't tell them apart. The mishnah doesn't grade the four out loud. Readers often point to the sieve, because sifting is a skill. Its fine flour is solet, the flour Leviticus names for offerings. Keeping isn't the goal. Choosing is.
screen: `SPONGE, FUNNEL, STRAINER, SIEVE.` · `THE STRAINER KEEPS THE DREGS.` · `THE SPONGE CAN'T SORT.` · `THE SIEVE CHOOSES.` · then, large: `KEEP THE FINE FLOUR.`

segments.voice: Sift today. Let three things you heard or read pass through: a headline, a comment, a passing worry, one at a time, on the out-breath. Then keep one fine thing from the day, a kind word, a good line, a small win, and hold it for the rest of the sit.
screen: `LET THREE THINGS FALL THROUGH.` · `KEEP ONE FINE THING.`

segments.voice: Sponge: the first of Avot's four students, soaking up everything at once. The sieve, last on the list, does the choosing.
Something to sift with: keep the fine flour, and let the dust fall through. Until tomorrow.

notes: Avot 5:15 paraphrased: four types among those who sit before the sages: sponge (absorbs everything), funnel (in one end, out the other), strainer (lets out wine, keeps dregs), sieve (lets out the flour dust, kemach, and keeps the fine flour, solet). Confirm.
'Readers often point to the sieve': commentators generally praise the sieve; the mishnah itself does not rank. Confirm.
